query: Do federal judges appointed by different Presidents (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic) differ in their voting tendencies on immigration injunction cases? Do Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration immigration policies compared to judges appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents?

schema.name: judge_name
schema.definition: The full name of the federal judge presiding over the case or issuing the order.
schema.rationale: Required to identify the specific judge and subsequently determine their appointing President.

schema.name: appointing_president
schema.definition: The U.S. President who appointed the judge to the federal bench.
schema.rationale: Directly addresses the core query comparing Trump-appointed judges with those appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents.

schema.name: case_name
schema.definition: The title of the lawsuit or legal action.
schema.rationale: Identifies the specific case being analyzed.
allowed_values: Darwin Antonio Arevalo Millan v. Donald J. Trump
Angelica S. v. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
Amica Center for Immigrant Rights v. U.S. Department of Justice
American Gateways v. U.S. Department of Justice

schema.name: challenged_policy_type
schema.definition: The type of immigration policy or executive action being challenged in the case.
schema.rationale: Helps categorize the nature of the Trump administration policies under review.

schema.name: injunction_ruling
schema.definition: The court's decision on the motion for a preliminary injunction or temporary restraining order.
schema.rationale: Measures the judge's voting tendency and supportiveness toward the challenged administration policy.
allowed_values: Granted in part / Denied in part

schema.name: supportive_of_administration_policy
schema.definition: Indicates whether the judge's ruling ultimately upheld or supported the Trump administration's policy position.
schema.rationale: Directly answers whether Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration policies compared to other judges.
